crambescin C1 exerts a cytoprotective effect on HepG2 cells through metallothionein expression induction.

crambescin C1 (CC1), a guanidine alkaloid from the sponge Crambe crambes, exerts a protective effect on HepG2 cells against oxidative stress by means of metalothionein induction and inhibits tumor cell growth at higher doses.

the marine sponge Crambescin A1 has a minor protective effect on tumor cells while crambescinin C1 exerts a protective effect against oxidative damage and also induces the arrest of the cell cycle in G1 phase.

the biological activities of CC1 and the molecular mechanisms involved in these effects.
